Abstract:

Rotor-bearing systems are critical components of rotating machinery, and their reliable operation requires effective condition monitoring and fault diagnosis. However, practical diagnosis is challenged by the difficulty of learning informative representations from vibration signals, class imbalance in fault datasets, and the occurrence of compound faults for which labelled training samples may be unavailable. This progress work therefore investigates deep learning-based approaches for intelligent rotor-bearing fault diagnosis under progressively challenging operating conditions. The first objective is to develop a physics-aware patch masking strategy for Masked Autoencoders (MAEs), using wavelet-derived frequency information and characteristic fault frequencies to improve representation learning from CWT scalograms for balanced multiclass fault diagnosis. The proposed Wavelet-MAE achieves 97.99% accuracy with only 5.7 M parameters, outperforming the considered state-of-the-art models in the evaluated setting. The second objective is to develop a generative deep learning framework based on VQ-VAE and PixelCNN to mitigate class imbalance through synthetic fault-sample generation. Under the considered imbalanced condition, data augmentation improves the average diagnosis accuracy from 94.39% to 97.68%. The third objective is to develop a multilabel framework for compound-fault identification and decoupling under zero compound-fault training conditions, where only single-fault samples are used for training. The proposed framework achieves 94.02% accuracy, 0.9789 F1-score, 0.9884 precision, 0.9790 recall, 0.0205 Hamming loss, and 0.0032 ranking loss, demonstrating its effectiveness in identifying unseen compound-fault conditions. Overall, the completed studies establish a progressive framework addressing representation learning, class imbalance, and compound-fault diagnosis in rotor-bearing systems.
